## Example 4.6 · Counting the terms {#ss4-example-4-6-b .ar-lesson .ar-summation-slide}

Evaluate the following expressions:

<div class="ar-summation-task"><span>b)</span><span data-math="\displaystyle\sum\limits_{k=4}^{15}5k">sum from k equals 4 to 15 of 5k</span></div>

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
$$20+25+30+\cdots+75$$

:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
$$\text{Number of terms}=15-4+1=12$$

:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 23 · Example 4.6(b)</p>

::: notes

First included term is 5(4)=20; last is 5(15)=75. There are 12 terms, not 15 or 11. Sum=12(20+75)/2=570. First click reveals the expansion; second reveals the inclusive count. The alternative S_15−S_3 also gives 600−30=570. Use a fresh first term 20 if applying the AP sum directly to the included block. This is the suggested pause if the lesson spans two periods.

:::
